$$
{\begin{aligned}5p+q=3 \\ 6p-\frac{1}{4}q=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}5p+q=3 \\ 6p-\frac{1}{4}q=-8 & |\,\times 4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}5p+q=3 \\ 24p-q=-32\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $q$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-q$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $q$-variable, and allows us to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5p+\cancel{q} & =3 \\ 24p-\cancel{q} & =-32 \\ 29p & =-29 \\ p & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $p=-1$ into the equation $5p+q=3$ to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5p+q & =3 \\ 5\cdot (-1)+q & =3 \\ -5+q & =3 \\ q & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $p=-1,\,q=8.$
